rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.4 - own field sampling of ~700 topsoil (0-10 cm) samples at 100 grid points in the saline-drip-irrigated shelterbelt, every two days over one 10-day irrigation cycle in July 2014 plus spring/summer/autumn sampling, analysed for moisture and EC with geostatistics. Q2: Abstract and Section 3.2.1, Figures 3-5 - under saline-water drip irrigation soil moisture declined during the 10-day cycle while soil EC rose from day 2 to day 6 then fell at day 8 and rose again at day 10 (rain); Section 3.2.2/Figure 8 - salinity slightly higher in summer than spring and increased from spring to autumn; abstract states long-time saline drip irrigation increased soil salinity slightly; share of non-salinized area dropped from 86% (day 2) to 54% (day 6). Q4: Section 3.2.1, Figure 4 - the intermediate variable (topsoil moisture depletion by evaporation between drip events) was measured concurrently with EC through the cycle, and irrigation water salinity (4.80 g/L) was measured. Q8: Section 3.2.1 - authors note light rainfall before the day-10 sampling confounded the end-of-cycle moisture and EC values and that the rain was insufficient to leach salt but may have washed salt from leaves to the soil surface.
rows.notes: The specific figures in the passage (moisture 27.4%->2.4%, 26.4%->2.7%; EC 0.64->3.32 and 0.70->3.99 dS/m for 15- and 10-day cycles) do not appear in this study; mean topsoil moisture here was 1.19% (max 10%) and mean EC 1.56 mS/cm, and only one 10-day cycle was sampled. The numbers must come from the other citation. This study supports only the qualitative pattern: moisture falls and topsoil EC rises during the first days after saline drip irrigation, then declines by day 8. Q3: single method (gravimetric moisture and 1:5 EC on soil samples) repeated over time; no independent method. Q5: one site, one Aeolian sandy soil, one shelterbelt. Q6: a single sampled section of the shelterbelt (~field scale), not a scheme or region. Q7: EC was correlated with silt/sand content and attributed to strong evaporation, but no condition is stated as a requirement for the effect. Q9: Table 1 gives SD and range for pooled EC and moisture across all samples but not for the within-cycle change itself; Figure 4 shows averages without reported dispersion; ANOVA significance only.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary field study of saline groundwater drip irrigation in a desert shelterbelt; evidence is observational within one irrigation cycle and three seasons of one year.
